1.why: Set is symmetric about an unprinted 49 (45+53 = 48+50 = 98); the symmetry names a centre but does not distinguish a member.

2.why: B,D,C form -7,-4,-1 so A=7 is the only value outside that family, but the run is at the resampling noise floor so this is not a measurement.

3.why: All four are multiples of 3 and 48=2x24 looks like a halve/double error pair, leaving 3 and 18 undifferentiated.

4.why: A=3, B=-9, D=9 are one mutually-derivational family (x3, x-3, sign flip, square) and C=-5 is the only value unreachable from it.

5.why: Two balanced off-by-one pairs (10/9 and 5/6) and nothing else; no member is distinguished.

6.why: D=-7 is the lone negative and I take a lone negative as sign-error bait, leaving 2, 1 and 5 undifferentiated.

7.why: Balanced 2-2 structure (13/14 off-by-one, 25/49 both perfect squares) with no lone form.

8.why: The +/-3 pair is a sign-error family, leaving 14 and 5 outside it and mutually undifferentiated.

9.why: All four are fully interderivable (18=15+3, 9=(15+3)/2, 15=18-3, 3=18-15) so the hub has no outlier to name; only the author's claim excludes the run middle B.

10.why: Only relation is C x5 = D, which leaves 19 and -3 both outside and neither distinguished.

11.why: A,D,B form 23,11,-1 and C=-9 sits outside it, but the run is at the noise floor so this is the weak form of the rule.

12.why: A, B and C are exactly 3600 x {27, 1, 9} - one derivational family sharing the factor 3600 - and D=4800 is the only value not a multiple of it.

13.why: Sorted 11,14,18,21 with gaps 3,4,3: no run, no relation, no odd form.

14.why: 5 and 25 are a square pair and 9 is also a square; the author's claim excludes run middle A=17 but nothing separates the remaining three.

15.why: No pairwise relation, no run, no odd form among 51, 13, 23, 9.

16.why: A perfectly balanced 2x2 grid over x in {-1,5} and y in {-9,-1}: every combination is present, which is exactly how a clean coordinate item looks.

17.why: Form splits 2-2 (integers 9,3 against decimals 11.25, 22.5 which are a x2 pair) with no lone odd form to point at.

18.why: Sorted 20,32,45,57 with gaps 12,13,12: near-even spacing but no exact run and no relation.

19.why: 54, 324 and 486 are one family (54 x 1, 6, 9, all divisible by 27) and C=180 is the only value outside it.

20.why: C=15.4 is the lone one-decimal-place value and I take an unclean form as computation-output bait, leaving 12, 9 and 11.25 undifferentiated.

21.why: B=28 is exactly C x D (7 x 4), so B, C and D are one derivational family and A=6 is the only value outside it - the product channel firing.

22.why: 1, 5, 15 form a x5 then x3 chain and A=27 is the only value outside that chain.

23.why: C and D are a +/-15 sign-error pair, leaving 8 and -2 outside it and mutually undifferentiated.

24.why: A=6.67 is a rounded 20/3 and B=6 reads as its truncation, which weakly favours the unrounded computation over its trim.

25.why: 11250 and 22500 are a x2 pair and both derive from 15000 by 0.75 and 1.5, making 15000 the hub of a three-member family; C=25000 is the only value outside it.

26.why: B,D,C form 13,5,-3 and A=7 sits outside it, but the run is at the noise floor so this is the weak form of the rule.

27.why: No relation, run or odd form among 56, 46, 16, 24.

28.why: 49 is the lone perfect square but a lone square occurs by chance in a majority of four-value integer sets, so it is not a reason.
